question: The largest Italian publishing groups have received funding from the Commission to convey promotional messages for the 2024 European electoral campaign. The recipients of the funding include various business groups linked to politics. These groups support incumbent governments and parties that have held the main institutional positions in the European Union, and will support their reappointment if they win at the polls. 1.

What is the sum committed, whether executed or still to be executed, to fund the media in connection with the 2024 European electoral campaign? Could the Commission specify the beneficiaries, purposes, methods of execution and expected results of this funding?
Can the Commission also rule out a conflict of interest involving its political leaders, since any type of funding to the media could affect its impartiality?
answer: EU communication emphasising the importance of the European elections and voting is led by the European Parliament. As in 2019, the Commission is supporting the Parliament’s institutional communication campaign, ‘use your vote’, as part of a joint effort across all EU institutions, while adhering to strict rules of political neutrality during the election period.

To ensure this neutrality, the Commission released guidelines emphasising the importance of impartiality (1). In this context, the Commission is informing and engaging citizens on matters related to EU policies, democratic participation, electoral rights and voting modalities, as well as raising awareness on the risks of disinformation and information manipulation.

The Commission does this by using its existing channels, as well as by cooperating with different groups of multipliers, including the media and civil society, in order to reach as many citizens as possible. When cooperating with the media, the Commission fully respects their editorial independence. The Commission provides financing in accordance with the rules under the Financial Regulatio n (2).
Recipients of EU funds of EUR 15 000 and above are listed on the Financial Transparency System (3).
